items.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
items.excerpt: Unlike other recent AI-generated proofs, this AI proof of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis has been unpacked and checked by human experts, and one mathematician calls the implications 'staggering.'

items.title: To detect deepfake videos, researchers turn to the physics of light
items.excerpt: An optical computing technique detects deepfake videos with a claimed 97.8% accuracy while using less energy than digital neural networks of similar performance.

items.title: PerturbAI and OpenAI launch AI reasoning agents for biomedical discovery
items.excerpt: A year-long collaboration between PerturbAI and OpenAI produced a reasoning framework in which thousands of agents turn perturbation datasets into testable biological hypotheses; the partners are now extending it to drug-target discovery on PerturbAI's causal data.

items.title: Forecasting 'tipping points' with AI climate simulation
items.excerpt: Caltech's Anima Anandkumar and colleagues at CU Boulder and NVIDIA used a recurrent neural operator to forecast abrupt tipping points, such as loss of ocean low clouds and a sudden drop in wing lift, in simplified models (PNAS).

items.title: AI designs functional enzyme components that could help expand drug discovery
items.excerpt: Researchers at HIPS Saarland combined pretrained AI models with lab experiments to design 76 new thiolation domains for non-ribosomal peptide synthetases; several worked in living cells and raised product yields up to threefold (Nature Communications).

items.title: Most AI chatbots stay in the political middle ground, with Grok being an exception
items.excerpt: Chalmers researchers had six LLMs write about 107 Swedish political issues before the 2026 election; most landed near the centre without favouring a party, while Grok diverged on migration, crime and gender (arXiv preprint).

items.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
items.excerpt: Participants rated even the most responsive AI as less conscious than the least responsive human, even when both behaved identically; asked about 'awareness' instead, they judged humans and AI far more similarly.

items.title: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
items.excerpt: Scientists used AI to map nearly 10,000 reactions in CO2-to-fuel conversion on copper catalysts, uncovering pathways traditional models missed, including a surprising hydrogen reaction that could inspire more efficient catalysts.

items.title: Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
items.excerpt: Google Research describes putting its Earth AI geospatial models to work through agents aimed at large planetary challenges.

items.title: Google Antigravity: accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides
items.excerpt: DeepMind shows Google Antigravity working as an agentic science workbench that discovers, structurally evaluates and prioritises novel antimicrobial peptide candidates in hours.

items.title: LitPivot: Developing research ideas through dynamic contextualization within the literature landscape
items.excerpt: Ai2's LitPivot helps researchers refine early research ideas through literature-supported critiques and revisions that update as a proposal evolves.

items.title: OlmoEarth v1.3: State-of-the-art embeddings for the whole planet
items.excerpt: OlmoEarth v1.3 brings state-of-the-art satellite embeddings, precomputed global data and a browser-based Embeddings Explorer for mapping and analysing the planet.

items.title: How Molmo 2's open release helped an MIT researcher rethink fish tracking
items.excerpt: MIT researcher Kai Van Brunt built Molmo2Fish on the open Molmo 2 model to track salmon in sonar footage and correct tracking errors using everyday language.

items.title: Should You Break Up With Your AI Boyfriend?
items.excerpt: A Psychology Today column asks whether AI romantic partners, which are becoming more common, are a healthy way to seek connection.

items.title: Low-power neural chip reads brain signals to identify cognitive and emotional states
items.excerpt: EPFL's LogSync implantable chip measures brain oscillations and cross-region synchrony and uses on-chip machine learning to classify cognitive and emotional states; it was tested on recorded human data and in rats (IEEE JSSC).

items.title: App's AI 'eyes' for blind users fall short, researchers find
items.excerpt: University of Maryland researchers analysed 418 conversations between 11 blind users and Be My AI and found answers often ran ten times longer than questions, forcing users to adapt their prompting (ACM CHI 2026).

items.title: AI chatbots often give unsafe or incomplete advice to survivors of tech-enabled abuse, study finds
items.excerpt: NYU Tandon tested 193 real survivor questions on GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet and two survivor-specific bots; 86% of answers fell short on accuracy, completeness or safety and 60% omitted critical safety warnings (USENIX Security 2026).

items.title: Researchers improve weather forecasts looking two to six weeks out
items.excerpt: An MIT-affiliated machine-learning 'wrapper' learns from a forecast model's past errors; applied to a leading European model it roughly doubled subseasonal accuracy and was the first to beat climatology in the two-to-six-week window.

items.title: Q&A: How AI came to model the 'messy' human mind
items.excerpt: MIT historian Benjamin Lindquist's Past and Present paper traces how early AI engineers injected randomness to mimic human creativity, and argues the same roots explain today's hallucinations.
